name: Green-breasted Mountain-gem
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of eastern honduras and north-central nicaragua
description: Medium-sized hummingbird, not particularly bright. Green above and dingy grayish below with dense green spots on sides and breast.

name: Brown-flanked Tanager
rangeDescription: Andes of central peru (huánuco, pasco, and junín)
description: Small tanager found in dry valleys in the Andes of central Peru. It is gray with a chestnut-orange hood, a buffy tinge to sides and vent, and a whitish belly.

name: Growling Riflebird
rangeDescription: Lowlands of central and southeastern papua new guinea
description: A large bird of lowland and foothill forest in eastern New Guinea. The bill is fairly long, slightly curved and more feathered in the base than its sister species.

name: Guianan Cock-of-the-rock
rangeDescription: Eastern colombia to southern venezuela, the guianas, and northern amazonian brazil
description: A large, chunky cotinga, always preceded by its reputation. Exquisite adult male is impossible to mistake for anything else; young males and females are brown and best identified by size, odd shape and pale eyes.

name: Cuban Tody
rangeDescription: Forest and woodland of cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: A small, gemlike, woodland species that is usually found in pairs. The rather large head, long bill, and short tail create a unique profile.

name: Hunter's Cisticola
rangeDescription: High mountains of western kenya, uganda, and northern tanzania
description: A large, plain cisticola with a reddish cap and two bands across the tail tip, one pale and one dark. Found in open montane habitats with thick herbaceous undergrowth, including forest edge, grassland, and heath, almost always in pairs or small groups.

name: Yucatan Poorwill
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (yucatán peninsula) to northern belize and petén of northern guatemala
description: Small dark nightjar of humid lowland forest in the Yucatan Peninsula, heard far more often than seen. Favors dense tangled forest, less often edges, and usually sings from a concealed perch.

name: Ridgway's Hawk
rangeDescription: Lowlands of hispaniola and satellite islands
description: A scarce small hawk of forests and open woodlands. The adult is very distinctive with its gray hood and barred orange belly.

name: Benguet Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern luzon (northern philippines)
description: A fairly small, slender bird of lower montane grassy valleys. Warm brown above and on the belly, with a white throat and a faintly streaked grayish chest.

name: Brown-chested Lapwing
rangeDescription: Range poorly known; breeds from nigeria east (probably) to northeastern democratic republic of the congo; disperses west to ghana, southward to cameroon and southern democratic republic of the congo, and eastward to western tanzania
description: Large, long-legged upland shorebird. Note the rufous above the bill and below the gray hood.

name: Henst's Goshawk
rangeDescription: Forest and savanna of madagascar (except central and far southern)
description: A big, powerful goshawk. Adults are gray on the back with fine gray barring below; females much larger.

name: Burmese Myna
rangeDescription: Myanmar and southwestern china (southwestern yunnan)
description: Medium-sized starling of forest edge, agricultural fields, and open scrubby or grassy areas. Thin, black bandit’s mask, medium-gray back, grayish-pink chest, dark iris and bicolored orange-and-black bill.

name: Streak-breasted Woodpecker
rangeDescription: Lowlands of myanmar and southwestern thailand to far northwestern malay peninsula
description: Medium-sized green woodpecker with delicate scale-like patterning on the underparts. Sexes differ primarily in crown color; male’s is red, female’s is black.

name: Pied Coucal
rangeDescription: New ireland and new britain (eastern bismarck archipelago)
description: A long-tailed, thick-billed, uniquely patterned bird with dark blue wings, tail, and belly and creamy neck, chest, and head. Note the obvious dark cap and mask.

name: Starred Wood-Quail
rangeDescription: Tropical forest of western amazon basin
description: Rotund brown bird of lowland rainforest understory. Reddish brown with small gray spots.

name: Gilbert's Whistler
rangeDescription: Southern western australia to northern victoria and southwestern and central new south wales
description: Chunky gray songbird with heavy black bill, found in dry forest and bushland across semi-arid southern Australia. Male has pale orange throat and dark, not orange, in lores (compare Red-lored Whistler).

name: Biak Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Numfor and biak (cenderawasih bay, off northwestern new guinea)
description: A fairly small bird of wooded areas on the Bay Islands. Low crest is flattened at the front and rounded at the back.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Benguet Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern luzon (northern philippines)
description: A fairly small, slender bird of lower montane grassy valleys. Warm brown above and on the belly, with a white throat and a faintly streaked grayish chest.

name: River Warbler
rangeDescription: Central and eastern europe to western siberia; winters in eastern africa
description: Large, rather nondescript warbler. Dark with a plain brown back, faintly streaked breast, and pale belly.

name: Andean Pygmy-Owl
rangeDescription: Andes from venezuela and colombia (including the sierra de perijá) through ecuador to northern peru (north and west of the marañón valley)
description: Very small owl of the upper subtropics and temperate forest. Typical pygmy-owl plumage: mostly brown or rufous above, white below with messy brown stripes, and small whitish spots on crown.
